person_note: The controlling narrator is the personified Truth, which introduces itself as "I" in q08084 and is described by Albom as the narrator of the whole book. Truth is treated as a character and ultimately connected to Fannie, so the controlling voice participates in the story under the methodology's definition of FIRST. The many aphorisms and generic uses of "you" are nondiagnostic, while third-person scenes about the other characters are recounted by that first-person controlling narrator rather than independently controlled sections. Confidence is medium because the decisive whole-book evidence is an author interview and reviews, while the authorized interior excerpt does not expose the narrator.
